publicationBoundary: Both figures come from one real teardown of one agent-installed tool on Anton's own machine. They support 'this class of tool re-installs itself from several places at once, so removal needs a gate not an edit'. They are a single incident, not a benchmark: do not frame either number as typical, as a vendor-wide property, or as measured across tools.

sources.headroom-teardown-rule: The write-back paths are enumerated in ~/.claude/conventions/workflow.md, 'Removing an agent-installed integration: kill the GATE, not the leaf': a 0.3s settings.json reconciler inside the running proxy, `init hook ensure` on SessionStart, the same on PreToolUse, a launchd KeepAlive, and managed shell-rc blocks. The gate they all consult is ~/.headroom/deploy/<profile>/manifest.json. Read 2026-09-12.

claims.note: Hero stat. Counted from the enumerated list, which names five mechanisms. Judgement call worth knowing: SessionStart and PreToolUse are the same `init hook ensure` mechanism on two triggers, so a stricter count reads 4. Five is defensible because each fires independently and each had to be disabled; if challenged, the honest answer is 'five trigger points, four mechanisms'.

Source line. Anton's own observed incident. Searched the local transcripts for a primary log of the hang and found no timing record, only later references to it, so this is classified as his report rather than verified. If a proxy log or session timestamp exists, promote it to primary and add the source.
